messages:
incident-bot: PAGER - SLO breach detected for customer `cobalt-ai` on prod: p95 latency > 2s and p99 > 6s over last 5m. Triggering paging policy. @maria_oncall you are oncall.

maria_oncall: Ack. Jumping in. Any immediate customer reports?

sam_support: Cobalt reported streaming stalls in their app, clients seeing partial chunks then stall. They say it started ~5m ago after a big batch of user prompts.

anya_sre: Observing p95 spike on route `/v1/generate` for tenant=cobalt with high concurrent connections. CPU on the dedicated-pool nodes is fine but GPU mem allocs show high KV cache churn.

joel_infra: I see many long-running requests (>= 30s) from that API key. Query pattern: repeated long prompts ~6k tokens. Concurrency peaked at ~900 qps for that tenant.

maria_oncall: Okay - looks like single-tenant overload + long sequence lengths. First mitigation: throttle concurrency on tenant to protect cluster. Joel, can you apply a temporary policy to cap concurrent requests per-key to 200?

joel_infra: Applying now. Command:```rdictl tenants update --id=cobalt-ai --concurrency-limit=200 --reason=\"emergency tail mitigation\"```

joel_infra: Done. New policy pushed to routing layer. Should be immediate-ish.

anya_sre: Seeing immediate drop in new inflight requests for cobalt. p95 trending down from ~2.6s to ~1.3s on aggregated hosts but p99 still high for in-flight long sequences.

maria_oncall: Next: fallback model routing for very long prompts. Can we route requests with context length > 4096 to the quantized-llama-small variant which has better latency for long context?

joel_infra: Adding a route rule:```rdictl routing add-rule --match \"tenant=cobalt && context_tokens>4096\" --target quant-llama-small --priority=1000```

joel_infra: Rule added. We'll monitor for mispredictions.

sam_support: Heads-up: Cobalt PM asked for ETA and has users stuck in workflows. I'm drafting an outbound note to let them know we've throttled concurrency and added fallback routing; will push update once we confirm improvements.

anya_sre: Found a reproducible pattern in traces: streaming stalls happen when model enters a pathological attention path for certain prompt templates with repeated nested code fences. KV cache growth + repeated cache fill causes GC-like stalls in the runtime at ~p50 token 1200.

maria_oncall: Can we temporarily disable streaming for that tenant to avoid partial chunk hangs? If we force non-streaming response we may pay higher token latency but avoid stalls. Any downside?

joel_infra: We can toggle per-tenant streaming off. Doing:```rdictl tenants patch cobalt-ai --streaming=false```

joel_infra: Streaming disabled for cobalt. Monitoring.

anya_sre: After streaming off + concurrency cap + fallback routing: p95 is now 1.1s, p99 down to ~3.2s. No new streaming stall alerts. Looks stable so far.

sam_support: Sent update to customer: \"We've applied a temporary concurrency cap and disabled streaming while we investigate. We're working on a lasting fix and will keep you posted.\" They replied: \"Thanks, reduction in errors but some user flows slower — ok for now.\"

maria_oncall: Great. Next steps: 1) Deep root cause — pinpoint why repeated code-fence prompts blow KV cache (assign to eng runtime). 2) Long-term control — autoscale policy per-tenant or soft-limits for very long contexts. 3) Post-incident writeup and RCA.

anya_sre: I'll collect traces and representative prompt examples (sanitized) and drop into the incident doc. Preliminary note: model runtime has a slow path when attention window contains many nested tokens that trigger decoder rescoring; looking into kernel dispatch behavior.

joel_infra: I'll prepare a short-term autoscale bump recipe for Dedicated pools: increase worker-count by +30% for tenant spikes detected by concurrency rules — can automate as a runbook.

maria_oncall: Handing off to @anya_sre for full investigation and @joel_infra for infra follow-up. I'll stay available for the next 2 hours. Please include a one-paragraph summary for next oncall.

eng-runbooks-bot: New runbook step recommended: \"tenant-tail-latency-mitigation-v1\" created and linked to incident.

any_sre-note: (typo: should be anya_sre) — corrected

anya_sre: Creating summary for handoff: \"Cobalt AI experienced a sudden surge of very long prompts causing KV cache churn and streaming stalls. Immediate mitigations: concurrency cap=200, streaming disabled, fallback routing for >4096 tokens to quant-llama-small. p95/p99 improved after mitigations. Investigations: runtime attention path + kernel dispatch for nested code fences. Action items: collect sanitized prompts, add telemetry for tokenized context length, and implement per-tenant long-context soft-limits.\"

maria_oncall: Good. Document that summary in pager duty handoff and mark incident as 'mitigated' but not 'resolved'.

sam_support: Customer asked for a post-mortem and whether we can provide allowed concurrency guidance. I'll onboard them to a dedicated-scaling proposal doc.

joel_infra: For tracking: added ticket INF-3342 (autoscale rules), RTE-789 (runtime kernel investigation).

maria_oncall: Offgoing note: I've paged and validated mitigations. Next oncall (in 2h) please continue trace analysis and coordinate with runtime eng. If customer impact resumes, escalate to SEV1.

eng-runbooks-bot: Handoff created to schedule: next_oncall=mike_tt at 1799002450.

maria_oncall: Ending live-ops thread. Thanks all.

anya_sre: I'll attach sanitized prompt corpus and initial flamegraphs to the incident doc.

sam_support: I'll close the customer-facing update once we have the RCA draft.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Links: traces: https://traces.internal/r/1799001234, runbook: https://runbooks.internal/tenant-tail-latency-mitigation-v1
